faqs.question: What do Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of abnormal cells, infectious agents, and other substances in the fluid collected from the peritoneal cavity.

faqs.question: Why are Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method done?
faqs.answer: This test is used to • Diagnose and monitor peritoneal malignancies, like peritonitis. • Detect infections or inflammatory conditions affecting the peritoneum. • Assess response to treatment for peritoneal cancer, ovarian cancer, gastrointestinal cancer, and mesothelioma. • Determine the stage and spread of cancer in the abdomen.

faqs.question: When are Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if you have • Symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating, or unexplained weight loss. • A family history of peritoneal or ovarian cancer. • Been diagnosed with cancer and there is a suspicion of spread to the peritoneum. • Undergoing treatment for peritoneal cancer or monitoring its recurrence.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the test results are abnormal, it may indicate the presence of abnormal cells, infections, or other abnormalities in the peritoneal fluid.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: During the test: • You will lie down on an examination table, and a local anaesthetic may be applied to numb the area. • A small incision will be made in your abdomen, and a catheter will be inserted to collect the fluid. • The fluid will be sent to a laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: Before the test: • You may need to fast for a certain period of time prior to the procedure. • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, as some may need to be temporarily stopped. • Follow any other instructions provided by your doctor regarding drinking fluids or taking any special precautions. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside this test include: • Imaging tests like CT scans or MRI to assess the extent of disease • Biopsy of suspicious lesions or tumors found during the procedure • Blood tests to assess overall health, check for tumor markers, or detect infection

faqs.question: What are Peritoneal Washings by Conventional Method also known as?
What is peritonitis?
faqs.answer: Peritonitis is an inflammation of the peritoneum, which is a serous membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers organs within it. It is usually caused by infection, trauma, or other conditions such as appendicitis or perforated bowel. Symptoms include severe abdominal pain, fever, and nausea.
